description: Out-of-order execution decomposed via Tomasulo's algorithm + its modern descendants. The complete machinery: fetch/decode produces a stream; the rename stage maps architectural to physical registers; dispatch puts instructions in reservation stations; the ready instructions issue to execution units; results broadcast on the common data bus update waiting RS entries; the reorder buffer tracks completion; in-order retire updates architectural state. This is what makes IPC > 1 possible.

sub_mechanisms.name: rename_stage
sub_mechanisms.definition: Per-instruction lookup that maps the architectural destination register to a freshly-allocated physical register, and source operands to their current physical mappings.
sub_mechanisms.why: Decouples instruction identity from register names. Two independent instructions writing the same architectural register get different physical registers — no false dependency. The renaming map IS the OoO execution's enabler.

sub_mechanisms.name: physical_register_file
sub_mechanisms.definition: Pool of physical registers (200-400 entries) backing the renamed values. Each in-flight instruction owns one entry until it retires and the rename is committed.
sub_mechanisms.why: Larger than the architectural register count (16-32). The pool size limits how many in-flight instructions can be tracked — physical register file pressure is a real bottleneck on dense-FP code.

sub_mechanisms.name: register_alias_table
sub_mechanisms.definition: RAT: per-cycle map from architectural register names to physical register tags. Updated by rename; rolled back on mispredict.
sub_mechanisms.why: The 'current state' of renaming. Speculative state of the RAT lives in the rename stage; architectural RAT is updated on retire. Branch mispredicts roll back to a checkpointed RAT.

sub_mechanisms.name: reservation_station
sub_mechanisms.definition: Per-instruction entry queueing operands. When all operands arrive (from rename or from broadcasted results), the entry signals ready to issue.
sub_mechanisms.why: Decouples ready-to-execute from ready-to-issue. An instruction enters RS with some operands unresolved; sits there until they all arrive. The RS is the OoO scheduler's working memory.

sub_mechanisms.name: issue_wakeup
sub_mechanisms.definition: Each cycle, scheduler picks ready RS entries and issues them to functional units. Selection considers age (older first), unit availability, port pressure.
sub_mechanisms.why: The dispatch loop's core. Wakeup logic compares each RS entry's operand tags against broadcasted result tags; matching entries become ready. Scaling wakeup to large RS is one of the biggest power costs in modern CPUs.

sub_mechanisms.name: common_data_bus
sub_mechanisms.definition: Result-broadcast network. When an execution unit produces a result, it broadcasts (tag, value) to all RS entries; matching entries capture the operand.
sub_mechanisms.why: The 'tag matching' that lets multiple instructions wake up simultaneously off one result. Wide CDB lets multiple results broadcast per cycle. Power-expensive — wide CPUs have multiple parallel CDBs.

sub_mechanisms.name: reorder_buffer_entry
sub_mechanisms.definition: ROB entry: holds (instruction, destination physical register, completion bit). Allocated at rename in program order; retired in program order.
sub_mechanisms.why: Tracks 'completed but not yet retired' instructions. Maintains in-order semantics for retirement even when execution was out-of-order. ROB size = max in-flight instructions = max ILP reachable.

sub_mechanisms.name: retire_stage
sub_mechanisms.definition: In-order commit. Head of ROB checks if its instruction completed; if so, updates architectural state (RAT, memory) and frees the ROB entry.
sub_mechanisms.why: Maintains the program's apparent sequentiality. Software sees in-order execution; hardware reordered freely behind the scenes. Retire is the boundary where speculation becomes architectural fact.

sub_mechanisms.name: branch_misprediction_recovery
sub_mechanisms.definition: On mispredict, flush all in-flight instructions younger than the branch, restore the RAT to a checkpoint, refetch from the correct target.
sub_mechanisms.why: Mispredict penalty = pipeline depth × throughput lost. Modern CPUs save checkpoints of the RAT at each branch to enable cheap rollback. Without checkpoints, restoration would require traversing the ROB serially.

sub_mechanisms.name: memory_dependency_speculation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Load instructions may execute speculatively before earlier stores whose addresses haven't been computed. Predictor learns which stores typically alias.
sub_mechanisms.why: Store-load dependencies prevent loads from executing OoO. Speculating they don't alias lets the load proceed; on misspeculation (store actually does alias), the load + dependents are squashed. Critical for performance.

sub_mechanisms.name: store_buffer
sub_mechanisms.definition: Holds completed-but-not-retired stores. Their values are forwarded to in-flight loads that match the address.
sub_mechanisms.why: Stores can't go to cache until retired (might be squashed). Buffer holds them; loads check the buffer before going to L1. Store-to-load forwarding makes 'store immediately followed by load' efficient.

sub_mechanisms.name: load_queue
sub_mechanisms.definition: Tracks in-flight loads, their addresses, and ordering relative to earlier stores. Used to detect load-store ordering violations.
sub_mechanisms.why: If a load executed speculatively before a store and the store's address turns out to match, the load read stale data. Load queue detects this; CPU squashes the load + dependents and re-executes.

sub_mechanisms.name: scheduler_clustering
sub_mechanisms.definition: Modern CPUs split the scheduler into clusters (e.g., 4 integer schedulers + 2 FP). Reduces wakeup fanout per cluster.
sub_mechanisms.why: Single monolithic scheduler at width 8 has 8×N wakeup logic — expensive. Clustering reduces per-cluster fanout. Trade-off: ops bound to one cluster can't issue elsewhere. Modern designs (Zen, Apple Silicon) heavily cluster.

derivation_rules.name: tomasulo_algorithm_underlies_modern_ooo
if: a CPU implements register renaming + reservation stations + CDB + ROB
then: it executes Tomasulo's algorithm with in-order retire
derivation_rules.why: Tomasulo (1967) is the canonical OoO scheme. Modern CPUs add window size, port count, scheduler clustering, but the algorithm is identical. The ROB extension (1988) added precise interrupts.

derivation_rules.name: rob_size_caps_in_flight_instructions
then: at most N instructions can be in flight simultaneously
derivation_rules.why: Each in-flight instruction needs an ROB entry. When ROB fills, dispatch stalls. ROB size is a major IPC determinant — Apple M3's 670 entries vs Intel's 512 vs ARM Cortex-X's ~300 directly affects how much memory latency they can hide.

derivation_rules.name: memory_speculation_makes_loads_first_class
if: loads can execute speculatively past unresolved store addresses
then: they participate in OoO execution like compute instructions
derivation_rules.why: Without memory speculation, loads serialise after stores whose addresses aren't yet known. The OoO window shrinks effectively to the load wait. Memory speculation makes loads start their cache access early — hiding ~50% of typical memory latency.

derivation_rules.name: in_order_retire_preserves_software_semantics
then: software sees the same architectural state as if execution were sequential
derivation_rules.why: The OoO scheme guarantees in-order retire (not in-order execute). Exceptions, interrupts, debug see architectural state corresponding to a specific instruction boundary. Speculation is invisible above the retire boundary.

derivation_rules.name: scheduler_complexity_limits_width
if: scheduler wakeup complexity is O(N²) per cycle for N RS entries
derivation_rules.why: Each broadcasted result must compare against each RS entry. Scaling N hurts power + clock frequency. Clustering and split schedulers mitigate this; the wide-decode designs (Apple, Zen 5) all use clustered schedulers.
